questions.title: How is an over-the-remaining-balance refund rejected?
questions.question: When a merchant asks to refund more than is still left on a payment (for example $30 on a $50 payment that already had $30 refunded), every version refuses it and refunds nothing. Should the merchant's system be told this the same way as a badly formed request (such as a zero or negative amount), or as its own kind of rejection meaning "the request was valid but exceeds what can still be refunded"?

options.label: Same as a badly formed request
options.clarification: A refund request for more than the payment's remaining unrefunded balance is rejected with nothing refunded, using the same invalid-request error (HTTP 400) as a zero, negative, or fractional amount.

options.label: Its own rejection: exceeds what is left to refund
options.clarification: A refund request for more than the payment's remaining unrefunded balance is rejected with nothing refunded, using a distinct "amount exceeds refundable balance" error (HTTP 422), separate from the invalid-request error (HTTP 400) used for zero, negative, or fractional amounts.
